title: publication_reconciler.py: record published_blob_sha256 fingerprint + merging-actor-identity (merged_by_verified_human) check
evidence_refs: Built _fetch_pr_merged_by (single-PR gh api endpoint -- merged_by is null on the LIST endpoint used by _fetch_merged_prs, a real, confirmed-live API quirk), _fetch_readme_blob_sha256 (live README.md raw content at the PR's merge_commit_sha, sha256'd), and _fetch_fingerprint_fields wiring both into apply_reconciliation for BOTH the UNRECORDED_PUBLICATION write path (new) and a new IN_SYNC refresh path (new -- needed so the 28 already-recorded products get a baseline fingerprint too, not just future discoveries).

CRITICAL LIVE FINDING, investigated before writing the identity-gate code (per this mission's own 'verify a spec against real behavior first' discipline, TC-17's own precedent): phase6b S3.VII's literal mechanism ('checking the merging actor's GitHub identity is not the pipeline's own bot/token identity') is NOT exercisable in this repository. `gh api user` for the live GH_TOKEN resolves to babar-raza, the human maintainer's own personal account -- there is no separate bot/service identity. Sampled every real readme-refresh PR merge event available via the single-PR endpoint (3d/net #3, note/python #5, font/python #1 -- the exact REVERTED case the hard rule most needs to catch): all three show merged_by: babar-raza, identical to the token's own identity, with zero PR review-approval trail on any of them (checked live: reviews endpoint returns [] for both 3d/net #3 and font/python #1). Building an identity-gate on this non-signal would either always-fail (blocking every real publication, since every merged_by equals the token identity) or be purely vacuous (font/python's REVERTED classification is already correctly produced by the existing ancestor-reachability check in TC-15, not by identity).

Design decision made from that finding: merged_by_login is recorded as an AUDIT field only (informational, never gates a state transition) -- confirmed via a dedicated regression test (test_merged_by_login_identical_across_every_real_sampled_merge_never_gates) that font/python's REVERTED classification and apply_reconciliation's refusal to write are UNCHANGED by merged_by_login's value. published_blob_sha256/published_commit (structurally sound, independent of the identity question) ARE built and gate TC-17's regression check -- this is the real, valuable, buildable half of TC-41's original scope.

SECOND real bug found and fixed during live canary verification (not caught by unit tests, which used a mocked command runner): gh api's `-f ref=<sha>` silently defaults the request to POST instead of GET unless `--method GET` is also passed, producing a 404 against the GET-only /contents/README.md endpoint. Confirmed live against the real 3d/net repo (both the failing -f form and two working forms -- --method GET, and embedding ref= directly in the URL query string -- tested side by side). Fixed by using the URL-query-string form (simpler, no extra flag).

Live canary, read-only (no --apply against the real registry -- that write is left for a human-reviewed follow-on, per this mission's own discipline of disclosing before mutating shared registries): 3d/net (IN_SYNC) and note/python (IN_SYNC) both correctly resolve published_blob_sha256/published_commit/merged_by_login against real GitHub data after the query-string fix; font/python (REVERTED) resolves the same fields when queried directly for illustration, but apply_reconciliation's existing REVERTED short-circuit (proven by test_reconcile_reverted_when_merge_commit_unreachable_real_font_python_case, unchanged) means these are never written for it regardless of merged_by's value.

9 new/updated tests in test_publication_reconciler.py (_fake_gh_runner extended for the 2 new gh call shapes; test_apply_reconciliation_writes_additive_fields extended to assert the new fields; test_apply_reconciliation_tolerates_fingerprint_fetch_failure -- a gh failure on the NEW calls must never break the already-proven core write; test_apply_reconciliation_refreshes_fingerprint_on_in_sync; test_apply_reconciliation_in_sync_noop_without_resolvable_pr_or_repo -- replaces the old is-noop test, same assertion, updated name; test_merged_by_login_identical_across_every_real_sampled_merge_never_gates -- pins the live finding as a permanent regression test).

title: Resume (was PAUSED, parent mission): live-published-regression gate + registry-drift-requeue trigger, safe design
evidence_refs: check_live_published_regression (readme_refresh_checks.py) compares the CURRENT live upstream README blob against the RECORDED published_blob_sha256 fingerprint (TC-41, data/readme_published_state.json) -- never the local candidate. This is the exact fix for the conflation the parent mission proved harmful: the pre-existing _published_readme_current_findings (readme_refresh_run.py, MT056) compares live README against the LOCAL CANDIDATE, which fires on every product with a disclosed-but-unpushed local improvement (the normal state of most of the portfolio) -- a naive hard-gate promotion of that comparison regressed 23/28 already-correctly-published products when tested live in the parent mission. The new check never touches the local candidate at all (its own signature has only registry_row/current_blob_sha256 -- pinned by a structural regression test, test_check_live_published_regression_never_touches_local_candidate), so that failure mode cannot recur.

Live-network orchestration kept separate from the pure check, preserving the offline/deterministic check-battery design boundary (same split reconcile_publications()/publication_reconciler.py already established): fetch_current_readme_blob_sha256(family, platform) (scripts/pipeline/lib/publication_reconciler.py) fetches the CURRENT live README on the default branch with no ref pinned -- reused _fetch_readme_blob_sha256 (TC-41, already fixed the -f-vs-query-string gh 404 bug) rather than reimplementing gh-fetch mechanics, only widening its ref parameter to optional. live_published_regression_portfolio() (readme_refresh_run.py) + new CLI subcommand `live-published-regression --family/--platform|--all [--json]` orchestrate per-product: skip the live fetch entirely when no published_blob_sha256 is recorded yet (checked=False, no network call -- pinned by a test asserting the fake gh runner raises if invoked), else fetch live and call the pure check.

No hard gate anywhere: check_live_published_regression is advisory-only, and live_published_regression_portfolio is a standalone read-only reporting operation, never wired into approve()/push() or any state-transition path -- per this taskcard's own explicit instruction not to promote without live proof.

Built _extract_salient_tokens_tagged/_extract_salient_tokens_split (new) splitting into literal_tokens/descriptive_tokens; _extract_salient_tokens itself is now expressed in terms of the tagged extractor with zero behavior change (pinned by test_extract_salient_tokens_unchanged_for_every_token_shape across 6 real excerpt shapes).

CRITICAL LIVE FINDING (would have invalidated a naive implementation): cells/typescript's own stored salient_tokens field does NOT match its own excerpt when mechanically re-extracted (31/31 mismatches) -- this product's own disposition ledger was hand-authored prose ("formulas", "styles", "Clone", "install"), not composer-mechanical output, unlike pdf/java (0/153 mismatches) and note/python (6/148). Building the naive literal_tokens-only check on cells/typescript still showed 61% zero-match (11/18) -- the schema split ALONE did not fix it. title: Resume (was PAUSED, parent mission): package-version currency gate, manifest-parsing scope only
evidence_refs: Confirmed live before writing any code: data/package_registry.json carries NO version at all for any product on the current scout mechanism -- every entry with scout_source starting package_manifest.py: has candidate.version=None; only 2 stale, pre-migration legacy rows (cells/java, cells/rust) carry a version at all, and even those disagree with the real manifest (cells/java registry row says 26.5.0, real pom.xml says 26.7.0, and the README's actual composed text already correctly says 26.7.0 -- confirming the registry is stale, not the content). This exactly matches the parent mission's disclosed PAUSE evidence and confirms the manifest-parsing scope decision was correct.

Built resolve_manifest_version(family, platform, clone_cache) in scripts/pipeline/lib/input_manifest.py (TC-13's module, extended not forked) -- per-language dispatch to net/dotnet (.csproj <Version>, test/sample/example paths excluded via deterministic sort so filesystem iteration order never matters), java (pom.xml scoped to the ROOT <project> element's own direct-child <version>, not a <parent> block's or a dependency's -- proven with a fixture that deliberately puts a parent version first; build.gradle fallback), python (pyproject.toml [project].version, dynamic=["version"] + [tool.setuptools.dynamic].version.attr resolved via AST-safe module inspection -- never exec()s anything, [tool.poetry].version, setup.py AST-first with regex fallback), typescript/javascript/nodejs (package.json), rust (Cargo.toml + nested/workspace fallback matching package_manifest.py's own established convention), cpp (CMakeLists.txt with real multi-location search, not just repo root), go (explicit out-of-scope). Returns {version, source_path, source_field} on success or {version: None, reason: ...} on a legitimate miss; never raises.

CANARY (mandatory acceptance criterion) PASSED: resolve_manifest_version('pdf', 'net', ...) live-reproduces the already-manually-verified v26.8.0 from the parent mission's TC-31, reading the real src/Aspose.Pdf.Foss.csproj (correctly excluding the sibling tests/Aspose.Pdf.Foss.Tests.csproj, which has no Version tag at all).

Two real bugs found and fixed live while building the Java resolver, neither caught by a naive implementation: (1) every real pom.xml in this portfolio declares <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>, and Python's ElementTree.fromstring() raises ValueError on a decoded str carrying an encoding declaration -- fixed by reading raw bytes (pom.read_bytes()), which also correctly handles one product's (3d/java) leading UTF-8 BOM; (2) a naive "first <version> tag in the file" scan would be wrong for any real pom.xml with a <parent> block preceding the project's own version (not currently true for any of this portfolio's 4 Java products, sampled live, but a real, general correctness gap) -- fixed via ElementTree scoped to the root <project> element's own direct children only, proven with a dedicated fixture.

C++ decision (per the mission prompt's own explicit invitation to investigate and disclose): built _find_cpp_manifest with real multi-location search (root CMakeLists.txt first, then the shallowest non-test/sample/example CMakeLists.txt anywhere in the clone, deterministically sorted). Live-verified against all 4 real C++ clone caches: pdf/cpp and email/cpp (root-level, VERSION present, 1.0.0 and 0.1.0 respectively) resolve correctly; cells/cpp (no root-level CMakeLists.txt at all -- the search correctly finds the real nested Aspose.Cells.Foss.Cpp/CMakeLists.txt, excluding its sibling tests/ CMakeLists.txt, and correctly reports no VERSION field declared, since it genuinely has none); slides/cpp (root-level, no VERSION field) also correctly reports the explicit no-version-declared reason. All 4 real products verified, not just the 2 originally surveyed.

Go decision (per the mission prompt's own explicit invitation to investigate and disclose): live-verified pdf/go's real git-tag reachability nuance directly (git merge-base --is-ancestor v0.5.0 HEAD fails -- the tag is not an ancestor of the clone's current HEAD, so git describe --tags --always falls back to a bare commit hash, 2306eeb). Declared Go explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this pass rather than build a git-tag resolver that could silently return a misleading bare-commit-hash value -- disclosed alongside the live-registry deferral, per this taskcard's own explicit permission to make and record that call.

Wired manifest_version additively into resolve_input_manifest's returned dict, matching input_manifest.py's own established schema-evolution style (peer to clone_cache/enterprise_edition_target). Deliberately NOT wired into diff_manifests (and therefore never triggers approve()'s drift-forced-replan) -- a disclosed, deliberate scope boundary: a package version changing between compose and approve is normal product activity, not the silent-registry-correction incident class diff_manifests exists to catch (TC-13/TC-27a's own tex/python precedent). Pinned by a dedicated regression test (test_diff_manifests_ignores_manifest_version_drift_by_design).

Reused _split_into_sections and _UNPUBLISHED_PACKAGE_SIGNAL_RE (grepped for and found already existing, per the mission prompt's own instruction to reuse rather than reinvent) rather than building a second unpublished-detection mechanism. Advisory only (hard_gate=False), matching its sibling check's own posture, for the same class of reason: the manifest source has real, disclosed gaps (C++ no-version, Go out-of-scope, Python dynamic-version placeholder) a hard gate would wrongly punish a correct README for.

Live-verified against real, current candidate READMEs (reports/repo-presenter-regen-full/): pdf/net (26.8.0, matches both the --version and Version= cited tokens, zero findings), cells/java (26.7.0, matches both the Maven XML and Gradle short-form cited tokens, zero findings -- and independently confirms the README's own content is correct where package_registry.json is stale), cells/typescript, pdf/python, cells/rust, email/cpp (all real "not yet published" Installation sections, all correctly zero findings via the reused unpublished-signal), 3d/python (setup.py-sourced version, zero findings), cells/cpp (no manifest version resolved, zero findings).
